prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules bring a chosen protein to the ubiquitin-proteasome system for destruction, through bifunctional degraders and cereblon-directed molecular glues

statement.case_for: I have moved from B009 to B045 after the first-round exchange. Induced proximity is a design principle that can be stated in two sentences: a small molecule brings a target and an E3 ligase together, and the cell's own machinery removes the protein. It is supported by quantitative mechanism (ternary complexes, cooperativity, degradation kinetics) that independent groups have reproduced, and it makes targets without an active site reachable. The maturity objection raised by Aili, Chabes, Somfai and the chair is real for PROTACs but weaker than it first sounds, because the glue branch that Handa's cereblon work explains already delivers approved drugs at scale, so consequences are demonstrated and not only promised. The credit core is also clearer than in my own first choice: Crews and Deshaies for the concept and its first proofs, Handa for the target and mechanism of the glue strand. I would hold the citation to what these three did, the concept and the cereblon mechanism, and not claim the later optimisation work.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC is approved, so the concept is being recognised ahead of its clinical verdict. A three-name cap leaves out Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure), Gray, Sakamoto and Kim (first proof of concept) and Ito (cereblon with Handa), and each of those claims is credible. PROTACs and glues were discovered separately and a single citation can blur them. If the committee judges that the two strands cannot be honestly joined under three names, B069 is the safer prize and B009 remains the strongest consequence-led alternative.

responses.point: Sparr challenged my B009 trio: Cullis, Hope and Madden carry the earliest encapsulation and pH-dependent assembly science, while Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan added lipid design, and the story sits close to the 2023 mRNA prize.
responses.response: I said I would move toward whichever configuration had the more defensible record, and on reflection neither version of the lipid trio is clean. Cullis, Hope and Madden hold the priority for the principle; Cullis, Anderson and Langer reflect delivery to patients; MacLachlan's ionizable-lipid design is left out of both. I cannot name one discovery and three people without an arbitrary cut, and that is the point on which I now defer to you. I still hold that the impact is beyond dispute and that this is chemistry, which is why it stays as my first alternative.

responses.point: Aili prefers B045 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, wants the citation to say openly that it rewards the concept and cereblon, not the optimisation work, and himself notes that the glue branch is clinically mature while PROTACs are not.
responses.response: I now agree with that framing and have adopted your trio and your caution about wording. Your own observation on the glue branch is what resolves my earlier worry about maturity: cereblon-directed drugs are already in clinical use, so the consequence is demonstrated for one strand. I would still say plainly that the PROTAC strand awaits its clinical verdict. I also accept your caveat that excluding Ciulli and Gray is a judgment about what the citation honours, and I would not claim it is a verdict on who made the compounds work.

responses.point: Chabes keeps Handa over Ciulli in the third place because cereblon is different in kind, an independent route to degradation that explained a decades-old drug, and wants both strands in the citation.
responses.response: I agree and I think this is the decisive credit argument. Ciulli's structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work refine a concept that Crews and Deshaies had already proved, whereas cereblon is a second, separate mechanism, so replacing Handa by Ciulli would change what the prize is for. I also agree that Ito's omission is uncomfortable, since he shared the cereblon work with Handa, and that is a real cost of the cap. On B009, you argued the opposite, that attribution is the harder problem; after this round I accept that.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B069 for Buchwald and Hartwig, arguing the attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist, the record spans more than 25 years, and the 2010 prize left C-N coupling out.
responses.response: I do not dispute the maturity or the pairing, and I would not oppose B069 if the committee cannot settle the degrader trio. My difference is the one I held in round 1: it extends an area honoured in 2010 and the 2021 organocatalysis prize, so it meets my standard of something completely new less well. I also note that your own argument, that the ligand logic was tested against isolated intermediates and kinetics, makes it a real chemical achievement and not a scope expansion; that is why I list it as a second alternative.

responses.point: The chair sets out B045 as concept plus mechanism and asks whether Ciulli displaces Handa and whether recognition before an approved degrader is premature.
responses.response: My answer is that Ciulli does not displace Handa, for the reason Chabes gives, and that the absence of an approved PROTAC is a reason to word the citation around the principle of degradation and the cereblon mechanism, not around any single drug class. I would not accept a four-name solution because the cap forbids it. If the committee decides the two strands cannot be honestly joined, I would prefer to fall back to B069 or B009 than to cut Handa and restate the prize as a PROTAC-only award.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will recognise degraders before any PROTAC is approved; I cannot verify the current clinical status from here.
Whether excluding Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito can be explained without implying they did not matter.
Whether PROTACs and cereblon-directed glues can be cited as one achievement without blurring credit.
The Vancouver and MIT credit split for B009 still rests on my recollection of the publication and patent history.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate. My connections are Arieh Warshel (postdoc collaboration), the Uppsala ribosome community and committee colleagues, and none of the credited names falls in those groups. I have updated my first choice from B009 to B045 and have no tie to Crews, Deshaies or Handa.
